text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The deputy head of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) has surrendered to authorities and has given them details about the guerrilla group's bases, leaders and structures. A GIA statement condemned Redouane Makador as a traitor who it said gave himself up to the authorities last month. The GIA ordered its activists in Algeria and abroad to cut links with him.
Three suspected Moslem activists had been arrested in Britain thanks to information provided by Radouane to Algerian security officials who passed it on to British counterparts.
- President Liamine Zeroual, chairing the first cabinet of the new coalition government, urged the ministers to step up reforms and tackle unemployment.
- Foreign ministers from 11 Mediterranean countries will meet in Algiers on July 11-12 on cooperation.
- Seddik Debaili, leader of the secular opposition Socialist Forces Front, says the party will ask Zeroual to launch an intiative to restore peace.
